cards.explanation: The answer is a woman in labor. The prophecy asks why she's crying aloud, then says anguish grips her like a woman in labor (Micah 4:9). It's a picture of real pain that's hard to ignore. I once got stuck in a stamper rack and thought THAT was pain, friends. It was not even close.

The answer is True. The text says, “there you will be rescued; there the LORD will redeem you from the hand of your enemies!” (Micah 4:10). Babylon is the last place you'd expect a rescue to happen. Hearing "Babylon" and "rescued" in one breath is like a boss saying "you're fired" and "congratulations" in one sentence. The LORD does the redeeming, and He does it right there.

The answer is False. Micah 4:12 says they do not know the thoughts of the LORD or understand His plan. They gathered with their own plan in mind, saying “Let her be defiled…” (Micah 4:11). It's like showing up to a party sure you know what's going on, while everyone else is in on something you've never heard about, friends. The LORD's plan was a different one.

The answer is to rise and thresh. The text says, “Rise and thresh, O Daughter of Zion…” (Micah 4:13). Threshing is hard work, so this is a call to get up and move. The nations may think they came to stare, but Zion is told to stand and work.

The answer is to devote it to the LORD. The text says, “Then you will devote their gain to the LORD, their wealth to the Lord of all the earth.” (Micah 4:13). The wealth gets handed over, not hoarded, friends. It all goes to the One who is Lord of all the earth.

The answer is Bethlehem Ephrathah. The text says, “But you, Bethlehem Ephrathah, who are small among the clans of Judah, out of you will come forth for Me One to be ruler over Israel…” (Micah 5:2). A small town gets named, and the ruler comes out of it. It's small on the map and big in what's promised.

The answer is from the days of eternity. The text says this ruler's origins are “…of old, from the days of eternity.” (Micah 5:2). The town is small, but His origins go all the way back. That's a lot of history for one little place to carry, friends.

The answer is return. The text says, “then the rest of His brothers will return to the children of Israel.” (Micah 5:3). It happens after she who is in labor has given birth. Returning means people coming back, and that's the picture here, bakers.

The answer is True. The text says, “He will stand and shepherd His flock in the strength of the LORD…” (Micah 5:4). The strength behind the shepherding comes from the LORD. This ruler isn't doing it on His own power, friends.

The answer is that they'll dwell securely. The text says, “And they will dwell securely…” (Micah 5:4). A shepherd standing over the flock means the flock can settle down. Nobody has to keep one eye on the door, bakers.

The answer is peace. Micah says, “And He will be our peace when Assyria invades our land and tramples our citadels.” (Micah 5:5). Assyria is the nation invading in that verse. The ruler doesn't just bring peace, friends. He IS the peace.

The answer is False. Micah 5:6 says, “And they will rule the land of Assyria with the sword, and the land of Nimrod with the blade drawn.” Ruling a land is the opposite of fleeing it, friends. The verse ends with this line: “So He will deliver us…”
